explanations.14: The colon-equals syntax sets a default value only if the variable isn't already set — so if you've defined AI_TEST_BATS_IMAGE in your shell config, this line won't override it.
explanations.22: The :A suffix converts a relative path to an absolute path, so later comparisons work correctly even if you pass in something like '../folder'.
explanations.32: The :h suffix removes the last path component (like dirname), so we're walking up one level in the directory tree.
explanations.65: The :A suffix here converts both paths to absolute form so they can be compared properly, even if one is relative and the other isn't.
explanations.67: The command substitution captures the output of realpath into the variable rel, and the 2>/dev/null hides any error messages if realpath fails (which happens on non-GNU systems).
explanations.79: This reconstructs a relative path by concatenating the 'up' string (like '../..') with whatever comes after the common prefix in the target path.
explanations.94: This calls a helper function to find the relative path from the directory where the test file will be saved to the source file it needs to load.
explanations.100: The $(...) syntax runs _ai_relpath as a command substitution, evaluating it right there inside the here-document string.
explanations.116: The file:t:r syntax strips the directory and extension from a filename, so 'path/to/backup.py' becomes 'backup'.
explanations.120: This extracts the PHP namespace from the source file by searching for a namespace declaration line and removing the keyword and semicolon.
explanations.150: The -E flag enables extended regex syntax, and the pattern uses word boundaries ([^[:alnum:]_]) to avoid matching function names that contain these words as substrings.
explanations.165: This checks if the docker command exists and is runnable; 2>&1 redirects both error and output to /dev/null to suppress any messages.
explanations.180: The --user flag runs the container with your actual user ID instead of root, so files written inside don't become owned by root.
explanations.198: The --env flags set environment variables inside the container; PYTHONPATH=/code tells Python where to find your project's modules.
explanations.214: The :e suffix extracts just the file extension, so 'backup.sh' becomes 'sh'.
explanations.226: The :h suffix gets the directory name, and :t:r gets just the filename without extension and path.
explanations.249: The $(<...) syntax reads the entire file contents into a variable in one go, similar to cat but more efficient.
explanations.278: The || return 1 means if _ollama_query fails (returns a non-zero exit code), this function immediately exits with an error too.
explanations.282: This strips markdown code fence markers (like ```bash and ```) that LLMs often add even when asked not to.
explanations.291: The -r flag tells print to treat backslashes literally (don't interpret escape sequences), so your code doesn't get mangled.
explanations.321: The :A suffix converts the path to absolute form, and then we remove the root prefix from it to get a path relative to the project root.
